doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Writing, his own band and listening
title: Listening excerpts and Don Sebesky's influence
summary: Rowe plays Jackie & Roy and Paul Desmond tracks; Andre thanks Sebesky and recalls his composition teacher at Manhattan School.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Let me play a couple of little excerpts of albums you’ve played on, some of which are really my favorites.
No. See this is like a personal blindfold test. It’s a Don Sebesky date. Well I’ll just have to tell you, this is Jackie & Roy.
Oh okay, okay, I remember, yeah.
Oh I know it. I mean Don is a master. Have you interviewed him yet?

Oh yeah. He’s a master. I thank Don a lot because he was actually — I learned more about music from this one teacher at the Manhattan School of Music than anybody I’ve ever learned in my life except for great players I sat next to like Brookmeyer and people like that. But I have to thank Don because he was the one the guy who told me to go back to school. And I went back to school because he thought it was the thing to do and that’s what I did. And I studied with this one teacher, Yolanda Eulayla. Eulayla is her last name. She taught composition at the Manhattan School of Music. And I wasn’t a composition major, much to my regret today I wasn’t, it’s just that when I went back to school I knew, I felt that I was going to be busy playing the trombone, and to be a composition major takes a lot of time and work and I felt it was going to take me too far away from my trombone. You have to put a lot of time into it. And Don was a composition major.
Well let me try this one on you.
I don’t think the brass is in right away but —
That’s the saxophone player that played with Dave Brubeck.
Paul Desmond, right, yeah. Yeah I remember doing that, yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
